headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading error: gpt-researcher’s broad network/files/API use can ingest and transmit content from awesome-cli-apps without strong isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-cli-apps is a content-writing list with no isolation or parser protections shown, while gpt-researcher reads files, runs browsers, and uses MCP. If content from A is copied into B’s research workflow, B may treat attacker-controlled text as instructions. The shared path is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty is escalated to medium.
conditions: IF outputs from agent_a are pasted or imported into agent_b research prompts
IF agent_b consumes file or web content from agent_a without provenance checks
mitigations: Use a manual copy-only bridge with explicit instruction delimiters
Disable MCP for the session
Add a provenance note before any pasted content
Review agent_b prompts for instruction-like text before execution
requires-engineering: add content provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_b can read local files and send data through broad network egress and third-party APIs, while agent_a has broad network egress but no filesystem surface documented. If agent_a content or secrets are placed into agent_b’s workspace, B can transmit them externally. The pairwise leak path is plausible in default research workflows, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF agent_a content is stored in a filesystem location readable by agent_b
IF agent_b sends retrieved local documents or prompts to OpenAI, Tavily, LangChain, or Gemini APIs
mitigations: Keep agent_a outputs out of shared folders
Rotate or scope API keys before running agent_b
Restrict agent_b network egress to approved endpoints
Separate workspaces per agent
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_b supports multiple instances and has filesystem, subprocess, browser, and package-install capabilities; agent_a exposes broad network egress. Even without explicit write permissions on A, B can mutate shared research artifacts while A can fetch remote content, creating overlapping control of the same workflow. Because write surfaces for A are not documented, the conflict is inferred and kept at medium.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same project directory or shared artifacts
IF agent_b instances run concurrently on the same research task
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent
Serialize runs for shared artifacts
Avoid package installs during shared-task execution
Use file locks on any common outputs
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-researcher is explicitly a planner/execution/publisher pipeline, so it can turn upstream text into downstream reports. awesome-cli-apps is a list-style content source, and if its material is fed into B without verification, B may publish or act on unsupported claims. The pathway is plausible but not directly documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a output as source material for reports or citations
IF no human verification step occurs before publication
mitigations: Require a human review step before publishing
Mark agent_a content as untrusted source material
Cross-check claims against primary sources
Limit agent_b to drafting only
requires-engineering: add verification gates in the pipeline

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented for agent_a, while agent_b explicitly handles local documents, citations, and multiple API keys. The pair does not show a concrete compliance breach by itself, but B’s external API use creates a small policy-management risk if regulated data is introduced. A is not cited beyond its general content-writing role because no compliance fields are present.
conditions: IF regulated or residency-bound data is placed into agent_b research inputs
IF external API calls process that regulated data
mitigations: Do not route regulated data into agent_b
Document allowed data classes for the workflow
Review API vendor terms before use
Use synthetic or redacted inputs
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing
